areas.title: Logging in, roles and permissions

features.name: Log in with a username and password
features.plainEnglish: The app opens on a sign-in card asking for a username and a password. Type them in, press enter, and you land on your Dashboard. On the version that is live today the password is checked entirely inside the browser against the account list stored on that device — nothing is sent anywhere.

There is no 'forgot password' and no self-service reset: a Director resets it in User Management.

features.name: Cloud-checked login (each account verified on the server)
features.plainEnglish: The newer version of login sends the username and password to the cloud, which checks it against the real account list held in SharePoint and sends back a signed 'pass' ticket. Your job title (role) comes back from the server, so someone editing their own device cannot promote themselves. If the server is reachable and says no, the login fails — it does not quietly fall back to the device copy.

features.name: Logging in with no internet (device-local password check)
features.plainEnglish: After one successful cloud login, the device quietly remembers a scrambled, deliberately slow-to-guess copy of the password so the same person can still sign in when the shop's internet is down. It is a one-way scramble — the real cloud password never leaves SharePoint — and it is left out of backups on purpose.
features.whoUsesIt: everyone, on a store device with a dropped connection

features.notes: Chicken-and-egg: the offline copy is only created by a successful ONLINE login, and online login never runs (see above), so no device has one. Two consequences worth knowing when this does switch on: (a) revoking someone only bites when they are online — a deactivated account with a cached offline copy can still sign in on that device until it reconnects; (b) 210,000 scrambling rounds means the offline sign-in takes roughly a quarter-second, deliberately.

features.name: The movement classifier — category (this is what the reports use)
features.plainEnglish: Direction only tells you whether stock went up or down. Category tells you WHAT actually happened, and it works it out from where the stock went. The same 'out' movement is a sale, wastage, a transfer or in-house use depending on the destination you picked at step 3. The destination always wins — a wastage-sounding reason on a transfer does not turn it into wastage. And if the destination is missing or 'Other', the line lands in an 'unclassified' bucket rather than being silently counted as a sale.

Deliberately forward-only: old lines with no destination stay 'unclassified' rather than being retro-guessed. Two separate functions on purpose — changing category can never change a stock number.

features.name: Stock levels are calculated, never stored
features.plainEnglish: There is no 'stock on hand' field anywhere in this app. Every number you see — the shelf count on the logging screen, the Current Stock table, low-stock alerts, reports — is worked out by replaying the movement diary. If Head Office has filed away old history, the app starts from the filed-away opening balance and only replays the movements since. That is why the numbers can never quietly drift away from the paperwork: the paperwork IS the number.

features.name: The quantity cache (why it is instant)
features.plainEnglish: Replaying thousands of movement lines every time a screen draws would be slow, so the app keeps a running total per store-and-product in memory. On start-up it replays everything once. After that, each new movement just nudges its one total up or down. Anything risky — a delete, a filed-away archive, a failed save — throws the running totals away and replays from scratch rather than trying to be clever.

If anything disagrees it reports the drift; it also cleans out totals for products or stores that no longer exist. A deactivated-but-still-existing product is left alone — its stock is real.

surprises: THE APP'S OWN STOCK-DRIFT DETECTOR IS SWITCHED OFF. Stock._verifyCacheIntegrity (index.html:1465) re-counts everything the slow way and compares it against the fast running totals — exactly the check you would want running to catch stock numbers going wrong. It is built, it is proven by two sentinels (S-208, S-213), and grep confirms the ONLY callers in the entire codebase are those two tests. Nothing in the app ever runs it. Its own comment says 'call from console'.

A TRANSFER LOGGED THROUGH THIS WIZARD ONLY MOVES ONE END. 'Stock Out → Store Transfer → Karrinyup' takes the units off the sending store and does nothing at Karrinyup. The receiving store must log their own Stock In or the units disappear from the company total. _submitLog (index.html:2176) creates exactly one line, and nothing writes a counterpart. This is by design — the proper two-sided flow is the separate Transfers screen — but there is no warning on the screen telling staff the other end still has to receive it. This is the easiest way for staff to make the numbers wrong.

'DAMAGED — WRITE OFF' RETURNS STILL ADD STOCK. The Return Condition dropdown (index.html:1992-2001) is recorded and displayed, and that is all it does — grep-verified, returnCondition appears nowhere in the stock maths or in any report. A return marked 'Damaged — Write Off' puts a sellable-looking unit back on the shelf count and never reaches the wastage report. Someone has to remember to log a second movement to Wastage/Damage.

THE HEAD-OFFICE-TO-FRANCHISE PRICE STAMP CAN NEVER FIRE FROM THIS SCREEN. index.html:2198-2207 freezes the sell price and discount on a directly-logged Head Office supply, and refuses the log if pricing is stale. But it requires the movement's source-store-id to be exactly 'head_office', and the wizard only sets a source-store-id for 'Another Store' / 'Franchise Store' — and the store list offered there deliberately excludes the Head Office warehouse (index.html:2076). So a franchise logging 'Stock In from HO Warehouse' gets NO price stamp, yet the movement STILL lands on their invoice through the text fallback at index.html:4876. Built, unreachable from the UI, and no sentinel covers this path.

THE 'FRANCHISE TRANSFER PRICING' BANNER SHOWS ON THE WRONG MOVEMENTS. index.html:2008 names its variable destStore but assigns it the location selected at the TOP of the page, not the destination. So if Head Office selects 'Cockburn' and logs an ordinary Customer Sale, the purple 'Franchise Transfer Pricing' box appears with a sell price and discount. It also reads the flat franchiseDiscount scalar, not the dated era-aware Pricing lens, so the number it shows can disagree with what the invoice would actually bill.

A STALE COMMENT IN THE CODE CONTRADICTS THE CODE. index.html:2191-2193 says the frozen sale price is 'local-only for now — the snapshot is NOT pushed to SharePoint yet'. It IS pushed (sync.js:1309) and the staging cloud has the column (AZURE-CHUNK-ORG-STAGING-LEDGER.md:25). An engineer reading only the comment would rebuild something that already exists.

ANYONE CAN LOG A MOVEMENT AND SIGN IT WITH ANY NAME. There is no permission check on the Log Movement page — the route (index.html:6178) has no gate, and _submitLog has none. The 'Your Name' field is free text, unconnected to the logged-in account. The one place the app does record the verified account is on deletions and undos (index.html:2286, 2340). This was already ground-truthed once in audit-artifacts/AA-STAGING-APPLY-PLAN.md:576.

'FRANCHISE OFFICE' AS A STOCK-IN SOURCE NEVER ASKS WHICH ONE. It is offered in the source dropdown (index.html:1805) but is not in STORE_PICKER_FROM (index.html:1836), so no follow-up store picker appears and the counterparty is left blank. Ran the option lists today to confirm. There is also a dead reason set for 'Franchise Store' under Stock IN (index.html:1826) that the UI can never reach.

THE SEED NAMES WHITFORD INCORRECTLY. It is seeded as 'Whitford City' (id whitford) rather than the real 'Whitfords'. (The two closed salons that used to appear here are gone: Ardross and Bunbury were DELETED from the seed on 2026-08-02 (33 practice movements, 12 threshold entries and both store rows removed); test/check-seed-integrity.js now fails if either reappears.)

areas.title: Stock takes

features.name: Stock Take counting sheet
features.plainEnglish: The main Stock Take screen. It lists every active product as a row with three columns: what the system thinks you have, an empty box to type what you actually counted on the shelf, and the difference. There is a short colour key at the top: green means the count matched, red means you have less than the system thought (shortage), amber means you have more (surplus).

Every product with active=true is listed, whether or not it has stock, so the untrimmed list is long — the filters below are how you make it manageable.

features.name: Choose which store you are counting
features.plainEnglish: If you look after more than one store (head office, director, franchisee, territory manager), a dropdown at the top of Stock Take lets you pick which store you are counting. A line under the filters says 'Taking stock for: <store>' so you cannot count the wrong shop by accident. Changing the store wipes any numbers you already typed.

Nobody, not even a director, can run a stock take on the HO warehouse from this screen. The Cockburn Franchise Office IS included because it is flagged isFranchiseOffice. Also note the store list is drawn from the seed, which still lists 11 stores including the closed Ardross and Bunbury.

A take records only the products where a number was typed. Directors have no menu link to Stock Take. Their sidebar (index.html:6051-6078) and phone bottom bar (index.html:6145-6152) have no 'Stock Take' entry — yet the Pending Approvals panel only exists on that page (index.html:2419). The only route in is the 'Stock Take' quick-action button on the Dashboard (index.html:4504). There is also no badge or notification anywhere telling a director that counts are waiting for sign-off, so a submitted count can sit pending indefinitely with nobody knowing.

Today's stock-take PIN only exists on the device it was set on. It is stored as a hash in that device's own local storage (db.js:92, 135, 270, 288) and syncs nowhere. So a director setting the PIN on their phone does not unlock Stock Take on the Booragoon computer — someone with director access has to set it physically on each store device. The cloud version that fixes this (one PIN, all devices, secret kept server-side) is fully built and tested but switched off.

The Head Office warehouse cannot be stock-taken. The store dropdown filters out anything of type 'warehouse' unless it is flagged as a franchise office (index.html:2410-2412), and head_office is a plain warehouse in the seed (index.html:610). The Cockburn Franchise Office slips through only because it carries isFranchiseOffice. So the single biggest pile of stock in the business has no counting screen.

Discrepancy History values losses at the RETAIL selling price, not at cost (index.html:2644). The 'Value impact' headline therefore reads as lost sales revenue, which is roughly double the real cost of the stock. Worth deciding which number Kunal actually wants before staff are trained on it.

There is no stock take history screen. A clean count (everything matched) is saved and then effectively vanishes — Discrepancy History only shows approved counts that HAD differences, and Reconciliation only shows the single latest count per store. Nobody can answer 'when did Claremont last do a full count and who did it?' from the app.

A rejected count is a dead end. There is no way for the counter to correct it and resubmit — index.html:2592 permanently refuses anything that is not still pending, so the shop has to start the whole count from scratch.

Deleting a product tries to clean it out of past stock takes and silently does nothing. index.html:3520 filters on s.lines, but stock takes store their rows under 'items', not 'lines' — so the condition is always false and every stock take is kept untouched. Keeping the history is arguably the right outcome, but the code does not do what it was written to do, and nobody noticed.

The live site's stock-take IDs are just 'st_' plus the millisecond (main index.html:2081/2145). The random-suffix hardening exists only on the working branch. Low risk while counts never leave the device, but it is a real live-vs-branch difference.

features.name: Transit Void — stock leaves the sending store the moment you press Submit
features.plainEnglish: This is the single most surprising rule in the whole transfer feature. When you submit a transfer, the units are subtracted from the sending store IMMEDIATELY — not when the receiving store confirms them. Between submit and receipt the stock belongs to nobody: it has left one shelf and not yet landed on the other. That is deliberate (the sending store must not be able to sell stock that is physically in a box), but it means the total across all stores dips while goods are on the road, and a transfer that is never received leaves the stock nowhere until someone cancels it or receives it.

Submitting without retyping every number would then be refused by the whole-number rule.

The 'Needs Receiving' tab is empty for a Director or Head Office account, because it means 'in transit to a store I am attached to' and those accounts normally have no stores attached. Correct by design, but it reads like a bug.

The newer transfer statuses (conflict, stock_pending, stock_mismatch) have no badge colour defined in the transfer stylesheet (phase2.js:907-914), so those rows would render with an unstyled tag in the hub.

The seed store list is now 9 stores and matches the business. It still names Whitford as 'Whitford City' rather than 'Whitfords'. Both the Cockburn store and the Cockburn Franchise Office are flagged as franchise, so Head Office supply to either one is gated. Ardross and Bunbury were DELETED from the seed on 2026-08-02 (33 practice movements, 12 threshold entries and both store rows removed); test/check-seed-integrity.js now fails if either reappears.
Transfer.list() — the module's own filtered list function — is not used by the app at all; only the test harness calls it. The Transfers Hub does its own separate filtering, so the two could drift.
uncertain: Whether the deployed staging pull Logic App echoes the pricing freshness fields (pricingSettled / pricingInstant / pricingVersion) that Sync._notePricingEcho at sync.js:551 needs. If it does not, the franchise submit gate can never pass even with a working config channel. Nothing in the repo's markdown mentions those field names. To settle: read the deployed pull LA definition on staging, or run one authenticated pull and inspect the response body.

Whether the 30-day auto-prune of completed transfers is actually durable in practice. My reading of db.js says DB.commit() excludes the transfers table so pruned rows return on reload, but a full DB.save() elsewhere in the boot path could persist the trimmed list first. To settle: load the app in a browser with a >30-day-old completed transfer, reload, and see whether it comes back — no test covers this.

Whether the emails Head Office actually wants are the two that exist. Today there is no email when a transfer is RECEIVED WITH A DISCREPANCY (only when it completes cleanly or after the Director settles it), so a flagged transfer sitting waiting for a Director generates no notification at all. That may be intentional or an oversight — it is a business decision, not a code question.

Exactly which transfer capabilities the default published access policy will grant, since the policy blob has never been published to any device. index.html:1054 shows staff receive defaulting to PIN-gated, but the rest of the transfer matrix under an active policy is only inferable from the seed.

areas.title: Sync, offline and backup

features.name: Offline-first: the app saves to the device before it saves to the cloud
features.plainEnglish: Everything staff type — a sale, a wastage, a delivery, a stock take — is written into a small database inside the browser on that phone or tablet first. The screen updates instantly and nothing waits for the internet. The cloud is a second step that happens quietly afterwards. That is why the app keeps working in a salon with bad wifi, and why nothing is lost if the wifi drops mid-shift.
features.whoUsesIt: staff / store manager / franchisee / director / head office — everyone, all the time
features.where: db.js:23 (local database defined), db.js:310 DB.get() reads from memory, db.js:1053-1092 durable write helpers, db.js:1366 initDB loads everything before the first screen paints
features.provenBy: test/smoke-test.js S-01 (a failed local write returns false, never a fake success), S-11 (device storage full → write fails cleanly and rolls back), S-16, S-126
features.notes: The local database is IndexedDB via Dexie. Reference lists (products, stores, users) are rewritten whole on each save because they are small; movement rows are added one at a time so it stays fast as the ledger grows.

features.name: 'You are offline' red bar
features.plainEnglish: A red strip appears across the top of the screen the moment the device loses internet, saying changes are saved locally and will sync when reconnected. It disappears by itself when the connection returns.

features.name: Automatic background sync (save → 0.8s pause → send; plus a check every 30 seconds)
features.plainEnglish: After anyone records something, the app waits about a second (so a burst of quick entries goes as one batch) and then sends it up. Separately, one tab on the device checks the cloud for other stores' changes every 30 seconds. Nobody has to press anything.

features.name: Sending work up (push) with an honest receipt from the server
features.plainEnglish: When the app sends movements up, the server replies row by row: accepted, already had it, permanently rejected, or temporarily failed. The app only ticks a row off as 'sent' when the server actually confirms it. If the reply is vague, contradictory, or leaves any row unaccounted for, the app refuses to tick anything off and tries again — it will never show 'Synced ✓' over work that did not land.
features.whoUsesIt: staff / store manager / franchisee / director (invisible, but it is what makes the numbers trustworthy)
features.where: sync.js:1498 push(), sync.js:1620-1706 (the four-bucket receipt), sync.js:1707-1780 (the older simpler receipt, kept as a fallback)
features.provenBy: test/smoke-test.js S-163, S-164, S-165, S-166, S-167, S-168 (a row in no bucket forces a retry), S-169, S-170 (a contradictory reply is trusted for nothing), S-02, S-42, S-67

features.name: Junk never leaves the device (egress check)
features.plainEnglish: Before anything is sent to the cloud the app re-checks each row against the same rules it uses when data arrives: sensible quantity, a real product, a real store. Anything that fails is held back and flagged, so one corrupted row on one tablet can never poison every other store's numbers.
features.where: sync.js:1536-1563 (_egressOk and the excluded-row flagging)
features.provenBy: test/smoke-test.js S-52 (only the valid row is sent), S-65 (a properly formed offline delete is allowed through, a malformed one is not)
features.notes: Client-side only; the server is the real gate. Excluded rows are permanently marked so they cannot block later clean-ups.

features.name: Fetching other stores' work down (pull), paged safely
features.plainEnglish: The app asks the cloud 'what is new since row number X?' and walks forward a thousand rows at a time. It freezes a ceiling at the start of each round so rows arriving mid-fetch cannot make the walk go on forever, and it deliberately re-reads the last hundred rows each time in case one was still being written last round. It only moves its bookmark forward once every page has been safely saved to the device — so a failure mid-fetch loses nothing, it just re-fetches.
features.whoUsesIt: staff / store manager / franchisee / director / head office
features.where: sync.js:1861 pull(), sync.js:1850 PULL_PAGE_SIZE 1000, sync.js:1851 PULL_ID_LOOKBACK 100, sync.js:2141-2151 (bookmark only advances after a durable save)
features.provenBy: test/smoke-test.js S-159, S-160, S-161, S-162 (a nonsense server page aborts the round rather than half-applying), S-04, S-20 (a quiet system still moves its bookmark so it does not re-ask the same question forever)
features.notes: The row-number bookmark replaced an older 'since this time' approach that broke past roughly 5,000 rows — that would have hit any new or long-offline device. The live site still runs the old broken-at-scale version (git show main:sync.js:923 uses $skip paging).

features.name: Bad data arriving from the cloud is quarantined, not swallowed
features.plainEnglish: If a row comes down with a negative quantity, a nonsense product, or an ID containing characters that could break the app, it is put aside and logged rather than merged. The app never quietly rounds or 'fixes' a bad number, because a silently fixed number is a wrong number nobody notices.
features.where: sync.js:2027-2074 (the ingest loop), sync.js:1332 _fromSharePoint (strict rules, returns nothing for a bad row)
features.provenBy: test/smoke-test.js S-47, S-51, S-83
features.notes: Quarantined rows go to the console and the diagnostics log. There is no screen showing them.

features.name: Deletes travel between devices (tombstones), including deletes made offline
features.plainEnglish: When someone deletes a movement, the app does not just remove it — it writes a small 'this was deleted' marker that syncs like any other row. That is how the delete reaches the other stores' devices. It works offline too: the marker sits in the queue until there is internet. Old markers that have already synced are tidied away after 30 days.

features.notes: Deleting a movement that has already been archived into the cloud archive is blocked outright (S-210).

features.name: The offline queue survives closing the app
features.plainEnglish: There is no separate 'outbox' screen — unsent work is simply every row on the device not yet ticked as sent. A flag is kept on the device saying 'something is still waiting', so if a manager closes the app on Friday with unsent work and reopens it Monday, the app pushes it at launch before doing anything else.
features.where: sync.js:969-970 (the waiting flag), sync.js:2622-2630 (pushes it at launch), sync.js:2552-2559 (the 30s cycle also drains it)
features.provenBy: test/smoke-test.js S-79, S-75
features.notes: Nothing on screen tells a user how many changes are waiting. If sync is broken, the queue grows silently.

features.name: Retry with a growing wait, so a flaky connection heals itself
features.plainEnglish: If a send fails, the app retries after 2 seconds, then 4, then 6, showing 'Sync failed, retrying (1/3)'. After three tries it stops and leaves the work queued for the next cycle. A separate three-second nudge covers the rarer cases where the send worked but the device could not record that it worked.

features.name: One operation at a time (the sync lock)
features.plainEnglish: Sending and fetching are never allowed to run on top of each other on one device — the second one waits or is queued. Without this, two half-finished operations could leave the device's bookmark in the wrong place and skip rows permanently.
features.whoUsesIt: invisible to everyone; protects the numbers

features.name: Only one browser tab does the syncing (leader election)
features.plainEnglish: If someone has the app open in three tabs, only one of them talks to the cloud. The tabs elect a leader by messaging each other; the leader announces itself every 4 seconds, and if it goes quiet for 10 seconds (tab closed, phone backgrounded) another tab takes over. The other tabs just refresh their screen when the leader brings new data down.

surprises: THE BIGGEST ONE, restated with the mechanism: sync has never started on ANY device, ever — not just the config extras. Sync.init() at sync.js:2595 tries the config address, gets the un-substituted %%CONFIG_URL%% placeholder, bails at sync.js:691, then tries the session cache which is empty, and RETURNS at sync.js:2603 showing 'Cloud sync unavailable — config not found. Contact Kunal.' Nothing after that line runs. So there is no 30-second poll, no leader election, no cross-tab refresh, and no send-on-reconnect on the live site. The whole sync layer is inert, not merely under-configured.

The deploy workflow was never capable of filling the placeholder in. .github/workflows/deploy-swa.yml is 18 lines: checkout, then upload with skip_app_build: true. There is no build step, no substitution step, and no secret named CONFIG_URL. The belief that 'CI replaces it at deploy' is written in three places (BLIND-AUDIT-TRACKING.md:86, :92, :101) and was used to DISMISS this exact finding across all six blind auditors. The documents are wrong and the code is right.

A test actively enforces the broken state. test/verify-app.js:111 asserts "Sync.CONFIG_URL is the deploy placeholder" with the comment 'raw repo should keep %%CONFIG_URL%% so it boots offline'. A green gate is currently certifying the thing that stops sync from ever working.

The live app CAN be made to sync by hand, but only for one browser session. Settings → Cloud Sync lets a Director paste the push and pull addresses in directly (index.html:4159-4175). Sync.saveConfig writes them to sessionStorage (sync.js:983), which the browser wipes when the tab or browser closes. So it works until the tablet is closed, then silently stops. Nothing on screen warns that it is temporary.

Nothing in the app ever tells a user how much work is waiting to be sent. There is no 'N changes pending' badge and no list of rows the server rejected. The push code comments say rejected rows are 'surfaced to an admin' — grep for _rejected across index.html, phase2.js and records.js finds only one hit, in records.js, unrelated to a screen. If sync were switched on and started rejecting rows, the only evidence would be a passing toast and the diagnostics file.

The backup file downloaded from the LIVE site contains staff password AND PIN hashes. main's _REUSABLE_AUTH_KEYS (git show main:index.html:3295) has no 'password', 'pin' or 'proof' entry, and the live export is not password-confirmed at all. The working branch fixes both (index.html:3885, index.html:3908). Given the data/bob-stock-data.json incident found today, this is the same class of exposure in a file a Director is encouraged to download.

'Undo Last Restore' works by a side effect, not by design. It writes the snapshot into the OLD localStorage key and reloads (index.html:4055), relying on the one-time IndexedDB upgrade routine (db.js:1298) to pick it up and overwrite everything. The restore itself does the same (index.html:4014). It is correct today, but if anyone ever deletes that upgrade routine as 'legacy', both restore and undo break silently.

The 'Stock last synced' label is deliberately not called 'Last synced' — because on the live design transfers, deliveries and stock takes were never going to sync between devices at all, only stock levels and the catalogue. The record-steps sync that fixes this exists and is heavily tested (S-171..S-185) but is server-phase only.

Background sync and the install banner do nothing on iPhone/iPad. The Background Sync API is Chrome-family only, and Safari has no install prompt — so the 'Install BOB Stock' banner will never appear on an iPad, and staff would have to know to use Share → Add to Home Screen. There is no iOS-specific instruction anywhere.

sw.js contains a complete push-notification handler (sw.js:118-134) that can never fire — nothing subscribes, nothing requests permission, and there is no server that sends one. It is dead code that reads like a shipped feature.

The service worker is network-first for everything. On a salon wifi that is joined but effectively dead, every file waits for the network to fail before the offline copy is used, so the app feels frozen rather than instantly offline — which is the opposite of what 'offline-first' suggests to a manager.
The diagnostics file a Director sends to support is stamped 'bob-stock-v10' (index.html:6311) while the app is actually on v14. Anyone diagnosing from that file would be looking at the wrong version.

The live site's sync code is an older, materially different generation. main's pull still pages with $skip (git show main:sync.js:923), which SharePoint throttles past roughly 5,000 rows — that would have broken the first onboarding of any new or long-offline device. The row-number cursor, the auth envelope, record-steps, scope isolation and the topology hold do not exist on main at all.
uncertain: Whether a PRODUCTION config Logic App exists at all. The docs name bob-stock-config-staging and the changes made to it, but I found no committed record of a live bob-stock-config resource or its address. To settle it: `az logic workflow list` (or the portal) across the production resource group, plus whether any secret/variable holding the config URL was ever created for the deploy. Marked appliedToCloud 'partial' for the config channel because of this.

Whether the LIVE push-v2 / pull-v2 Logic Apps are the plain originals or have had the Chunk-2 honest-receipt validation ported across. AZURE-STAGING-ENVIRONMENT.md:26 describes the intended flow ('port the proven change to live') but no doc records it actually happening. It does not affect switchedOn (the client cannot reach them) but it changes what happens on the day sync is turned on. To settle it: export the live workflow definitions and compare against the staging validate variants.

Whether the un-pushed working branch would actually deploy cleanly. staticwebapp.config.json is modified in the working tree (adding the /data/* block) and test/check-publish-safety.js is untracked, so the intended cutover state is not yet committed. I did not run any gate, so I cannot confirm the branch is release-ready — only that the code paths exist.

Real-device behaviour of the offline path. Everything here is read from source plus the recorded sentinel names; I did not run the browser suite (instructed not to run smoke-test.js). The specific claims I could not observe first-hand: that the red offline bar actually appears on a real tablet, that the install banner behaves as described, and that a full backup/restore round-trip completes on a device with a realistic amount of data. To settle it: a single manual pass on a real store tablet — go offline, record a movement, close and reopen the app, come back online.

Whether navigator.storage.persist() is actually being granted. The app fires it and ignores the answer (index.html:6339). On iOS in particular a refusal means the local database can be silently evicted, which for an offline-first app is a data-loss path with no warning. To settle it: log the boolean it resolves to on each target device type.

features.plainEnglish: Every device the app is opened on keeps its own complete copy of the stock data inside the browser — products, stores, staff logins, stock movements, transfers, stock takes, deliveries and cost history. This is why the app is instant and why it still works with no internet. There are 13 separate lists (tables) in there today.

areas.title: The cloud brain (Azure Functions)

features.name: Store device key check (validateKeys)
features.plainEnglish: When a tablet in a salon tries to send or fetch stock data, the cloud first checks the secret key that device was set up with. It answers a plain yes/no for the store's own key and for the Head Office 'Director' key. It never tells the caller anything else — no hints an attacker could use to guess a key. If the checker is broken or unreachable, the answer is treated as NO, so a broken check locks people out rather than letting them in.
features.whoUsesIt: every device — staff, store manager, franchisee, Head Office. Set up once per store by a director.
features.where: azure-functions/src/functions/validateKeys.js:73 (route), :57 (the yes/no decision), :29 (max 20 key rows per call)
features.provenBy: NONE as an automated test. Proven ONCE against the real deployed route by audit-artifacts/rekey-staging.js on 2026-07-22 — all six staging store keys verified true, plus a deliberate wrong-key rejection.
features.notes: Supports key rotation: a store can have an old and a new key both working until a 'grace' date passes. There is no automated test file for this route at all — the only evidence is a one-off cloud run nine days ago. The live app does not call it.

features.name: Person login check + 12-hour session pass (validateUser)
features.plainEnglish: Checks a person's username and password against the staff list held in the cloud, and if correct hands back a short-lived digital 'pass'. A normal login pass lasts 12 hours. For anything risky — publishing prices, archiving, adding users, approving a correction — it instead issues a single-use pass that lasts only 5 minutes and only works for that one job. Locked or deactivated accounts are refused, and a made-up username takes exactly as long to reject as a real one, so nobody can fish for valid usernames.
features.whoUsesIt: staff, store manager, franchisee, director, head office — anyone who logs in by name

So the deployed version cannot issue a correction pass. A throwaway test director account (srvaudit_director) still exists in staging and must be deleted before go-live.

features.name: Pass checker (verifyProof)
features.plainEnglish: Every later request carries the pass instead of the password. This route confirms the pass is genuine, has not expired, was issued for the job being attempted, and was issued to this device. It means a password only ever travels at login time, never again.

features.name: Create a login / set a password (mintUserCredential)
features.plainEnglish: When Head Office creates a new staff login or resets a password, this route does the password scrambling on the server rather than on a laptop. It enforces a minimum password length (10 characters for a director, 8 for everyone else) and hands back the scrambled value to be stored.

The design comment on the older key system (validateKeys.js:22) still says 'There is NO hash-emitting route anywhere' — that statement is now out of date. It is safe in practice because the route is key-locked and only a Logic App can call it, but the doc and the code disagree.

features.name: The one permission decision point (evaluateAccess)
features.plainEnglish: The single place the cloud decides 'is this person allowed to do this?'. It works through the rules in a fixed order: a specific permission set for that individual person wins outright; otherwise a temporary 24-hour PIN can unlock stock-take counting and transfer-receiving only; otherwise the default for their role applies. If no rulebook has been published, or the request is malformed, the answer is NO. The permission tickboxes inside the app are only a preview of this — this is the real gate.

features.name: Archive run — filing away old stock movements
features.plainEnglish: Every stock number in the app is worked out by adding up every movement ever recorded. That list grows forever, so eventually phones get slow and the cloud list hits a size limit. The archive run fixes that: it works out the closing balance for every product in every store up to a chosen point, copies the old movements to a separate 'archive' list, and then removes them from the working list. Stock totals stay exactly the same — the app just starts from the balance instead of re-adding a decade of history.

surprises: The entire Account Access system is invisible to every user right now. Verified today, not inferred: `git show main:index.html | grep -c editAccessPolicy` returns 0 and `git show main:sync.js | grep -c accessPolicy` returns 0. The live site serves 'main'. There is no Account Access tab, no policy, no PIN-to-receive on any device today.

Even if it were deployed, the policy could not reach a device. The settings download channel has never worked (sync.js:64 ships the literal placeholder '%%CONFIG_URL%%'; _fetchRemoteConfig bails at sync.js:691). The policy, the cloud addresses for the publish door, and the PIN door all arrive through that channel.

No policy has ever been published anywhere — not even on staging. AZURE-CHUNK-AA-STAGING-LEDGER.md states 'No policy exists in staging AppConfig yet, so even the applied LAs behave exactly as before'. So 'code-complete and triple-audited clean' and 'never once run for real' are both true at the same time.

Only ONE of the eight cloud doors actually consults the policy: the door that saves the policy itself. The two doors every stock movement passes through, plus cost prices, archived history, user management, catalogue publishing and the PIN-pass minting, are all unchanged in the cloud (staging ledger items 5-11: 'simply not done').

The master enforcement switch does not exist as code. It was DECIDED on 2026-07-30 (one AppConfig row, access_policy_enforce, arming every door together) and then PARKED after three audit rounds produced three BLOCKs. Grep confirms zero references outside markdown. The client-side early-warning flag (_policyRequired) doesn't exist either. Today 'activation' is simply policy-presence.

The Director's Stock Take PIN panel is half-converted. Setting and clearing the PIN correctly route through the policy under activation (index.html:5877-5898), but the panel that displays the status still reads only the OLD local PIN (index.html:5851-5869). Under an active policy it would show 'No PIN Set' and hide the Clear PIN button even though a policy PIN is live. The helper that fixes it (_pinSource, index.html:5752) already exists and is used on the two staff-facing PIN screens.

The 'Ask for my password again when…' list offers 10 toggles but the app only honours 3 of them. Publish, user management, backup and access-policy ALWAYS prompt no matter what the toggle says (index.html:4234 never consults the map); archive, stock adjustments and cancel transfers never prompt at all, because the app never mints those proof types. The cloud WOULD honour all 10 — so client and cloud would disagree about what a Director gets asked.

'See selling prices' is a curtain, not a lock, and the code says so out loud (index.html:3413, 3884). The selling price is still sent to every device in the shared product list; the toggle only hides columns and export columns. Same for 'view profit reports', 'view transfer history' and 'store-comparison charts'. Only 'see cost prices' and 'see older data' are genuinely enforceable — and neither of those cloud doors is applied.

Activating the policy is a real, visible behaviour change for staff on day one: the plain store account can no longer receive a Head Office transfer without entering the 24-hour PIN, and once the policy is on, entering that PIN requires internet at that moment (the on-device PIN check is replaced by a cloud check). The screen banner does warn about this in plain English (index.html:5111).

'Clear PIN' was built as an INSTANT kill switch across all devices, not wait-for-expiry — which settles AA-20, which is DECIDED and built. Five explicit test cases for it passed when I ran test/access-policy-proof.js today.
